Claim 1 (Currently Amended): A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising one or more logic circuits, each logic circuit configured to: receive a plurality of independent first entropy values from a hardware source; apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value; seed a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value; generate a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

Claim 2 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

Claim 4 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware source is a ring oscillator, and at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator.

Claim 5 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware source is a single hardware source, and at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source.

Claim 6 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware source is a plurality of independent hardware sources, and at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent hardware sources.

Claim 7 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a permutation function, and at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

Claim 3 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to: implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number in which a key is produced; and produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

Claim 8 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 7, wherein at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to: divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values; apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

Claim 9 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a hash function, and at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

Claim 10 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

Claim 11 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

Claim 12 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein at least one of the one or more logic circuits is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.

Claim 13 (Currently Amended): A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising: receiving a plurality of independent first entropy values from a hardware source; applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value; seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value; generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

Claim 14 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

Claim 15 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes at least: implementing a key-agreement protocol using the random number in which a key is produced; and producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

Claim 16 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware source is a ring oscillator, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator.

Claim 17 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware source is a single hardware source, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source.

Claim 18 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware source is a plurality of independent hardware sources, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent hardware sources.

Claim 19 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a permutation function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

Claim 20 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 19, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes: dividing the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values; applying the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and concatenating the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

Claim 21 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a hash function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

Claim 22 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

Claim 23 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes selectively applying multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

Claim 24 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.
